quests.instruction: Rice grows best with its roots in plenty of water. Which kind of place suits it best?
quests.correctAnswer: Warm places with plenty of rain 🌧️
options: Warm places with plenty of rain 🌧️
quests.hint: Think about flooded fields.
quests.explanation: Rice grows well where it is warm and there is plenty of rain or river water. A freezing desert or a windy mountaintop does not suit it.
quests.funFact: Farmers flood rice fields to help the plants grow and to keep weeds down.

quests.instruction: Which tree crop thrives in the warm, dry summers around the Mediterranean Sea?
quests.hint: Its fruit is pressed for oil.
quests.explanation: Olive trees love the sunny, dry summers of the Mediterranean. Maple trees like cold forests and coconut palms like tropical beaches.
quests.funFact: Olive oil is a key ingredient in many Mediterranean dishes, from Greece to Spain.

quests.instruction: What fruit grows best in hot tropical lands rather than in cool places?
quests.hint: It needs warmth all year round.
quests.explanation: Mango trees need warmth all year. Apples and cherries need cooler weather.
quests.funFact: Apples and cherries need a cold winter rest each year, but mangoes do not.

quests.instruction: Which drink comes from the leaves of a plant grown on cool, misty hillsides in places like India, China and Sri Lanka?
quests.hint: The leaves are picked and dried.
quests.explanation: Tea leaves grow well on misty hillsides. Orange juice comes from fruit and hot chocolate comes from cocoa.
quests.funFact: Cool mist and slopes on tea hillsides slow the growth of the leaves, which helps them develop flavor.

quests.instruction: In very cold northern lands where few crops can grow, which foods have long been important for many families?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what the cold seas offer.
quests.explanation: Where it is too cold for most crops, fish and other foods from the sea have long been important. Mangoes, bananas and rice need warmth.
quests.funFact: Many northern peoples have traditional ways of drying and smoking fish to keep it through winter.

quests.instruction: Why are fish and seafood main foods in many island countries?
quests.correctAnswer: Seas full of fish surround them 🌊
options: Seas full of fish surround them 🌊
They have no water nearby at all 🏜️
They have far too much farmland 🌾
quests.hint: Look at what surrounds an island.
quests.explanation: Islands are surrounded by sea, so fish and seafood are easy to catch and eat.
quests.funFact: Fish and rice meals are common in many island and coastal communities.

quests.instruction: Where winters are long and cold, which traditional methods have people used to keep food for months?
options: Leaving it in the sun all day ☀️
quests.hint: Think about ways to stop food from spoiling.
quests.explanation: Pickling, drying and smoking keep germs from growing, so food lasts through winter.
quests.funFact: These old methods are why many cuisines have pickles, dried fish and smoked meats.

quests.instruction: Which preserving method uses lots of salt to draw water out of fish or meat?
quests.hint: It stops germs from growing by removing water.
quests.explanation: Salt pulls water out of food, which makes it hard for germs to grow. Whisking and steaming do not preserve food.
quests.funFact: Salted fish has been traded around the world for hundreds of years.

quests.instruction: Cabbage is packed with salt and left to ferment until it turns sour. What is the result?
quests.hint: It tastes tangy.
quests.explanation: Fermented cabbage becomes sauerkraut. Coleslaw is raw and cabbage soup is cooked.
quests.funFact: Helpful bacteria make fermented cabbage sour and help it keep for months.

quests.instruction: Tomatoes, potatoes and chili peppers all first grew in the same part of the world. Where was it?
quests.hint: Think about foods travelers found more than 500 years ago.
quests.explanation: These three crops first grew in the Americas and were carried to other continents.
quests.funFact: After reaching Europe, potatoes became staple foods in places like Ireland and Poland.

quests.instruction: Which fiery plant from the Americas spread to Asia and Africa and now flavors many dishes there?
quests.hint: It makes your mouth feel hot.
quests.explanation: Chili peppers came from the Americas and spread around the world. Black pepper and garlic came from other parts of the world.
quests.funFact: Before chilies arrived, many Asian cooks used black pepper and ginger for heat.

quests.instruction: When people move to new places, they bring their foods with them. What can this create?
options: Foods that all taste exactly the same 🍞
Foods that nobody enjoys any more 😕
quests.hint: Ask yourself what happens when two cooks share ideas.
quests.explanation: When people share foods and ideas, they often blend them into brand new dishes.
quests.funFact: Many popular dishes, from Korean tacos to pizza with local toppings, come from blending traditions.

quests.instruction: Which round pastry with a sweet filling is shared with family during the Mid-Autumn Festival in China and nearby countries?
quests.hint: Its shape matches the full moon.
quests.explanation: Mooncakes are round pastries shared at the Mid-Autumn Festival. Bagels and waffles are not part of it.
quests.funFact: Mooncakes are round like the full moon, a sign of family togetherness.

quests.instruction: Which treats are often shared with family and friends during Diwali, the festival of lights?
quests.hint: They are sweet and colorful.
quests.explanation: Mithai are sweets shared at Diwali. Pretzels and pickles are not sweets.
quests.funFact: Mithai come in many shapes and flavors, such as ladoo and barfi.

quests.instruction: Which sweet fruit do many families eat first to end the daily fast during the month of Ramadan?
quests.hint: It grows on palm trees.
quests.explanation: Dates are sweet and give quick energy, so many families eat them first. Lemons are sour and chilies are spicy.
quests.funFact: Dates are among the oldest cultivated fruits in the world.

quests.instruction: Which cool, creamy yogurt drink, served sweet or salty, is popular in India and Pakistan?
quests.hint: It is made from yogurt.
quests.explanation: Lassi is a yogurt drink. Hot chocolate is made with cocoa and lemonade is made from lemons.
quests.funFact: Mango lassi blends yogurt with ripe mango.

quests.instruction: Which fried dough sticks rolled in sugar are popular in Spain and Latin America, often dipped in thick hot chocolate?
quests.hint: They are long and ridged.
quests.explanation: Churros are fried dough sticks with ridges. Bagels are chewy rings and waffles are cooked in a press.
quests.funFact: Churros are often eaten at breakfast or as an afternoon snack.

quests.instruction: Which chilled tea drink with chewy tapioca pearls began in Taiwan?
quests.hint: It is sipped through a wide straw.
quests.explanation: Bubble tea mixes tea, milk and chewy pearls. A smoothie is blended fruit and coconut water is the liquid in a coconut.
quests.funFact: The chewy pearls are made from cassava starch.

quests.instruction: You are a guest and are offered a dish you have never seen. What is a polite way to respond?
quests.correctAnswer: Say thank you and try a little 😊
options: Say thank you and try a little 😊
Refuse it and leave the table 🚪
Say it looks and smells disgusting 😖
quests.hint: Think about how the cook would feel.
quests.explanation: Saying thank you and trying a little is kind and shows respect for the cook.
quests.funFact: Being a polite guest at the table is valued in cultures around the world.

quests.instruction: In many parts of the world people eat with their hands. What is a respectful thing to do first?
quests.hint: Clean hands touch the food.
quests.explanation: Washing your hands keeps the food and the meal clean for everyone.
quests.funFact: In many cultures a bowl of water or a sink is placed near the table for washing hands before the meal.

quests.instruction: A classmate does not eat a certain food. Which is the kindest way to think about it?
quests.correctAnswer: There may be many reasons for it 🌍
options: There may be many reasons for it 🌍
They have never tried real food 🍽️
quests.hint: Think about all the reasons a family might choose foods.
quests.explanation: There can be many reasons, such as health, beliefs, allergies or family customs, and they deserve respect.
quests.funFact: Families choose foods for reasons such as health, allergies, faith and tradition.

quests.instruction: A country has a long coastline and many fishing towns. Which foods are most likely to be common there?
quests.hint: Ask yourself what boats bring in.
quests.explanation: Where there is a long coast, fish and seafood are close at hand. Pineapples and mangoes do not grow in snow.
quests.funFact: Coastal cuisines around the world feature fish, from Japanese sushi to Portuguese grilled sardines.

quests.instruction: A land of wide grassy plains is perfect for raising cattle and sheep. Which foods are likely to be common there?
quests.hint: Think about what grazing animals give us.
quests.explanation: Grassy plains support herds of animals, so meat, milk and cheese are common. Rice and coconuts need different conditions.
quests.funFact: Grassy plains in places like Mongolia and Argentina have long traditions of herding animals.

quests.instruction: A hot, wet tropical land has rich, rainy soil. Which crops are likely to grow there?
quests.hint: Think about plants that love heat and rain.
quests.explanation: Bananas, coconuts and cassava thrive in heat and rain. Wheat, barley, oats, apples, pears and cherries prefer cooler weather.
quests.funFact: Tropical lands also grow cacao, coffee and many spices.

quests.instruction: Why do many families pass down their favorite recipes?
options: To prove who cooks the very best 🏆
To make cooking much harder to do 😵
quests.hint: Ask yourself what a dish can remind you of.
quests.explanation: Family recipes carry memories and traditions from one generation to the next.
quests.funFact: Many cooks learn recipes by watching and helping family members rather than reading a book.

quests.instruction: Which Moroccan cooking pot has a cone-shaped lid that lets steam rise and drip back into the stew?
quests.hint: The lid is shaped like a little hat.
quests.explanation: A tagine's cone lid keeps the stew moist as it cooks slowly. A wok and a griddle look different.
quests.funFact: The word tagine names both the pot and the stew cooked in it.

quests.instruction: Which round-bottomed pan used in Chinese cooking heats quickly for stir-frying?
quests.hint: Its curved sides help cooks toss food.
quests.explanation: A wok's shape lets food cook fast over high heat. A tagine cooks slowly and a baking tray is flat.
quests.funFact: A wok's shape lets cooks toss food quickly and cook it in just a few minutes.

quests.instruction: Which pair matches a food with the kind of place where it grows well?
options: Bananas and the icy, frozen tundra 🍌
quests.hint: Match each crop with its climate.
quests.explanation: Potatoes grow well in cool highlands. Bananas and coconuts need warmth.
quests.funFact: Climate, soil and rain decide which crops can grow in a place.

quests.instruction: Which dish uses an ingredient that first came from the Americas?
quests.hint: Think about tomatoes.
quests.explanation: Tomatoes first grew in the Americas, so a tomato sauce uses an ingredient that traveled across the world. Rice and wheat grew in other regions first.
quests.funFact: Many dishes we think of as traditional use ingredients that traveled the world long ago.

quests.instruction: What is a good way to learn about foods from another culture?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask questions and taste with respect 🙋
options: Ask questions and taste with respect 🙋
Assume everyone eats the same way 🙅
quests.hint: Ask yourself how to be a good guest.
quests.explanation: Asking questions and tasting with respect helps you learn. Laughing or assuming does not.
quests.funFact: Food is one of the friendliest ways to learn about other cultures.
